result.summary: Read core-directives.md and security-invariants.md (all S1-S14) in full, docs/agents/design/REQ-030.md in full, then the actual diff myself (domain/walkin.ts, handlers/walkin.ts, domain/user.ts's getUserIdByPhone/createWalkinUser, domain/profile.ts's createWalkinProfile, index.ts's registration, i18n additions, and handlers/walkin.db.test.ts in full) -- not REVIEWER's report. S1 (task item 3, my OWN abandon scenario): traced makeWalkinCommandHandler (handlers/walkin.ts) end to end -- after parseWalkinArgs/getEventById/requireOrganizerForChapter/validateWalkinFields all succeed, the ONLY remaining action is ctx.reply(...) with the confirm message; commitWalkin (the sole write path into users/profiles/registrations, domain/walkin.ts) is never called from this handler. Grepped the whole diff for commitWalkin's call sites: exactly two, both inside handlers/walkin.ts's confirm and override callback handlers, neither reachable without an actual Confirm/Confirm-override tap. Independently re-ran the producer's own AC1 test (walkin.db.test.ts, real Postgres, confirmed NOT skipped -- dbAvailable's console.warn never printed and the file's 7 tests ran in 1.42s total, consistent with real short-lived DB round-trips, not an early t.skip() return): dispatches /walkin via genuine grammY bot.handleUpdate, asserts a confirm message with buttons was sent, then asserts zero rows in users/profiles/registrations (queried directly) because Confirm was never tapped. Crash-before-confirm scenario: since nothing is written until commitWalkin runs (which only ever runs from inside a tap handler), a process restart between the command and a Confirm tap leaves nothing to orphan -- there is no partial row, no draft table, no in-memory map for a restart to lose; this is trivially true by the same 'no write reachable before a tap' argument, not a separate code path I needed to exercise further. PASS. MESSAGE-TEXT-AS-STATE-CARRIER RE-DERIVATION (task item 4, independent, not trusted from the design gate): grammY's Context.callbackQuery.message is Telegram's own `maybeInaccessibleMessage`/`Message` object as delivered by the Bot API's `callback_query` update -- it is populated server-side by Telegram from the actual stored message content at the time of the tap, not client-suppliable. An ordinary Telegram user has no API surface to attach an inline keyboard to a message they send (only a bot's own sendMessage/editMessageText can attach `reply_markup`), and cannot rewrite the text of a message the bot sent (Telegram only allows the origin sender -- the bot, via its own token -- to edit a message it sent). So a `callback_query` whose `data` matches `walkin:confirm:` can only ever be attached to a message this bot itself rendered via formatWalkinConfirmMessage/formatWalkinOverrideMessage, for exactly the `eventId` embedded in that button at render time -- confirmed content-forgery is structurally impossible, matching the design gate's conclusion, re-derived independently rather than copied. My OWN adversarial cross-context scenario: could an organizer for chapter A, who also has access to (can see) a walk-in confirm/override message rendered for a DIFFERENT organizer's event in chapter B, forge a cross-context confirm by tapping that message's button? Traced both callback handlers (handlers/walkin.ts lines 162-242): the `eventId` used for EVERYTHING -- getEventById, requireOrganizerForChapter, and the commitWalkin call -- comes from WALKIN_CONFIRM_PATTERN/WALKIN_OVERRIDE_PATTERN matched against `ctx.callbackQuery.data` (the button's fixed payload), NEVER from the re-parsed message text; the design's own Open Question 6 flags the `Event:` line as purely cosmetic and this is confirmed true in the actual code -- `parseWalkinMessageFields` never returns an `eventId` field at all, and neither handler ever reads one out of parsed text. Authorization is then re-derived FRESH on every tap: `requireOrganizerForChapter(db, BigInt(tgId), event.chapterId)` re-reads the tapping user's own role/chapterId from `users` via `ctx.from.id` (the tapper's identity, not the original command-issuer's) and re-reads the event's REAL chapterId from a fresh `getEventById` call, then compares them. Consequence: even if organizer A could somehow see and tap organizer B's confirm message (e.g. both present in a shared chat), the authorization check evaluates A's own role/chapterId against the message's OWN eventId's real chapter, and organizer A -- not being organizer for that chapter -- is refused with 'wrong-chapter', exactly as if they had typed the command themselves. No value from the message text ever substitutes for or weakens this re-derivation; the message text supplies only `name`/`company`/`phone`, which are inert data fields with no authorization role. Re-authorization happens at all THREE of the command/confirm/override entry points (§4 of the design, confirmed in code at handlers/walkin.ts lines 65, 186, 228), never trusted from an earlier tap. PASS -- cross-context forgery is refused by the ordinary authorization gate regardless of message visibility, and is separately impossible to construct in the first place because Telegram will not let a non-bot party attach a matching callback_data to arbitrary content. S2 (task item 5): confirmed by direct code read that `requireOrganizerForChapter` (domain/eventAuthorization.ts, REQ-016, confirmed ABSENT from `git diff --name-only master...HEAD` -- byte-for-byte unmodified) is the ONLY authorization call anywhere in domain/walkin.ts or handlers/walkin.ts; grepped the whole diff for `requireEventStaffForEvent`/`EventStaff` -- zero hits. Independently re-ran the producer's own AC6 test (real DB, real dispatch): an EventStaff member for the event (explicitly seeded with an EventStaff row but role='member'/wrong chapter) invokes /walkin directly and is refused with `notAuthorized`, no confirm message sent, zero rows written. Verified the check is re-run, not cached, at all three entry points (command handler line 65, confirm handler line 186, override handler line 228 of handlers/walkin.ts) -- each independently calls getEventById then requireOrganizerForChapter against a freshly-read event.chapterId. PASS. S7/S8 STALENESS AND ATOMICITY (task item 6): read commitWalkin (domain/walkin.ts) directly. Every call opens its own `db.transaction`, locks the events row with `.for("update")` (line ~238), locks any existing registration row with `.for("update")` (line ~273), and computes `admittedCount`/`seatsLeft` via `countAdmittedRegistrations`/`computeSeatsLeft` INSIDE that same locked transaction -- never a value carried over from an earlier tap or an earlier read in the handler. This directly answers the staleness question posed: if the event fills up between the confirm tap's message being rendered (which happened, if at all, on an EARLIER call to commitWalkin from a PRIOR confirm/override tap) and a later tap, the later tap's own fresh locked read picks up the current state -- there is no code path where a decision from an earlier call is reused for a later write. The override path (`overrideConfirmed: true`) recomputes `seatsLeft` fresh and independently decides the audit action (`registration.walkin_admit` if a seat actually freed up, `registration.walkin_override_admit` only if still genuinely full) via the exact `seatsLeft > 0` check at write time (domain/walkin.ts line 337), not from any earlier confirm tap's now-stale calculation. Exactly one `writeAuditLog` call exists on the only two writing branches (`check-in-existing-admitted` and `admit-and-check-in`), both inside the same transaction as the row mutation; every non-writing outcome (event-not-ready/cancelled/finished/already-checked-in/needs-override-confirmation) returns before reaching either write. Independently re-ran the producer's own AC3 tests (real DB): confirming an at-capacity override writes admission='admitted' + exactly one audit_log row with action='registration.walkin_override_admit'; dismissing the override offer (Dismiss button, shared cancel handler that never calls commitWalkin) leaves zero registration rows. PASS. S11 (task item 7, primary focus, my OWN full-diff grep): `grep -n "log\.\|console\.\|logger\." apps/bot/src/domain/walkin.ts apps/bot/src/handlers/walkin.ts apps/bot/src/domain/user.ts apps/bot/src/domain/profile.ts` -- zero calls to any logging function anywhere in the new/changed code (the only 'log'-shaped hits are unrelated identifiers like `getCatalog`/`catalog.walkin.*`). Read every `writeAuditLog` call site directly (domain/walkin.ts lines ~323-330 and ~376-383): payloads are exactly `{ eventId, source: "walkin" }` and `{ eventId, previousAdmission, source: "walkin" }` -- `phone` (and `name`/`company`) are never keys in either literal object, structurally, not by a redaction step applied after the fact. Read writeAuditLog itself (domain/auditLog.ts) -- it inserts exactly the caller-supplied payload with no additional field-copying that could reintroduce phone. Read the success-message interpolation (handlers/walkin.ts handleWalkinCommit, lines 128-134): only `parsedFields.name`/`parsedFields.company` (via companyPlaceholder) are interpolated into `catalog.walkin.success` -- `parsedFields.phone` is never referenced anywhere in handleWalkinCommit's reply construction. PASS for the log/audit-payload half of S11. DISPLAY-VS-LOGGING DISTINCTION (task item 7, second half): formatWalkinConfirmMessage/formatWalkinOverrideMessage DO render the raw phone into the confirm/override-offer message text, and parseWalkinMessageFields reads that same raw phone back out on every subsequent tap. I agree with the design's own reasoning (§10) that this is NOT S11's negative case, for a reason I verified independently rather than accepted on assertion: S11's own wording scopes the invariant to 'plaintext logs... application logs, error traces, audit payloads, and anything echoed into a Telegram message to a THIRD PARTY' (security-invariants.md S11). The confirm/override message is a direct reply in the same conversation/chat the organizer just typed the phone into, addressed back to that same organizer -- it is not a third party, and not a log, error trace, or audit payload; it is the functional mechanism (§1.1) that makes this flow's confirm/cancel/override round trip possible at all without a session store. This is the same class of exception REQ-019's formatProfileDump already establishes and this SECURITY-REVIEWER gate accepts it for the identical reason: showing collected data back to the person who supplied it one message earlier, in the same chat, for their own confirmation, is categorically different from persisting or transmitting it to logs/audits/other users. Grepped `writeAuditLog`/`log\.`/`console\.` call sites specifically for any argument built from `ctx.callbackQuery.message.text` or `parsed.fields.phone` -- zero hits; the re-parsed phone is used ONLY to pass through to commitWalkin's `args.phone` (eventually into profiles.phone, which is a designed, consented storage column per S1, not a log) and is never separately logged or audited from the handler layer. PASS -- S11's actual negative case (grep phone out of process logs and every audit row after a walk-in) is satisfied: it appears in neither. PHONE-MATCH FALSE-POSITIVE DISCLOSURE (task item 8, new PII concern posed): read commitWalkin's person-resolution step (domain/walkin.ts lines 249-262) and handleWalkinCommit (handlers/walkin.ts lines 99-157) together. When getUserIdByPhone finds a match, the flow proceeds using the MATCHED userId, but every subsequent reply to the organizer -- the success message, the override-offer message -- interpolates ONLY `parsedFields.name`/`parsedFields.company`/`parsedFields.phone`, i.e. the door-collected values the organizer JUST TYPED, never any field read back from the matched user's existing profile row (matchedUserId's own firstName/company/phone are never selected or referenced anywhere after the match -- confirmed by reading getUserIdByPhone's return type, `Promise`: it returns only an id, no other columns, so there is nothing of the matched person's existing data available to leak even if a handler wanted to). So a false-positive phone collision (design's own flagged §3.3 tradeoff: two different people sharing a normalized phone) does NOT disclose the wrongly-matched person's identity or any of their stored fields to the organizer at the door -- the organizer only ever sees back what they themselves typed. The residual risk is a DATA-INTEGRITY one, not a disclosure one: a registration/admission gets silently attached to the wrong existing User/Profile row, which is the exact tradeoff the design already names and accepts (§3.3), not newly introduced or worsened by the implementation, and not covered by any AC. Not a FAIL of this gate. PASS on the disclosure question specifically asked. OBSERVATIONAL NOTE (non-blocking, pre-existing, not specific to this diff): formatWalkinConfirmMessage's phone-display reasoning above assumes the /walkin command is issued in a private (organizer-only) chat. I checked the whole apps/bot/src tree for any chat.type/private-chat restriction on command dispatch (`grep -rn "chat.type" apps/bot/src`) and found none anywhere in the codebase -- this is a pre-existing, bot-wide structural assumption (every command, including REQ-019's already-reviewed formatProfileDump precedent) that commands run in a 1:1 chat with the bot, not enforced in code, not introduced or worsened by REQ-030. Flagging for ORCH's awareness rather than blocking this gate on it: if /walkin is ever run in a group chat containing other members, the phone would be visible to everyone in that group, not just the organizer who typed it. This is structurally identical to every other PII-echoing reply already in this codebase and was not re-litigated by this gate since it predates REQ-030 and no acceptance criterion for this requirement concerns chat topology. MIGRATION SIGN-OFF (S13 trigger check): `git diff master...HEAD --name-only` and a direct diff of `apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts` both confirm ZERO migration files and ZERO schema.ts changes in this diff -- verified directly, not by trusting the design doc's 'Schema: NO CHANGE' claim (independently re-checked: `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts` produced no output). S13's migration-sign-off duty does not trigger; N/A, not silently skipped. REMAINING S1-S14 ITEMS: - S1: PASS (above) -- three consents never conflated: only `consent_pd_at`/`consent_pd_version` are written by createWalkinUser, no code path touches `broadcast_opt_in` or `publish_consent` anywhere in this diff (grepped, zero hits). - S2: PASS (above). - S3: N/A -- this flow never renders another person's Profile to a third party; the only person's data shown back is the door-collected values shown to the organizer who entered them (see S11 display/logging distinction above), and on a phone match, none of the matched person's own stored fields are ever surfaced (see false-positive disclosure analysis above). - S4: N/A -- no new token type introduced; `generateQrToken()` (REQ-020, unchanged) is reused exactly as-is for the walk-in's own registration row, same generation path already reviewed under prior requirements. - S5: N/A -- no check-in-refusal/scan flow touched by this diff. - S6: PASS -- both writing branches (`check-in-existing-admitted`, `admit-and-check-in`) set `checked_in_at` only together with (or already alongside) `admission='admitted'` in the same UPDATE/INSERT statement; no branch sets `checked_in_at` while admission is anything else. - S7: PASS (above). - S8: PASS (above). - S9/S10: N/A -- no notification/broadcast send introduced by this diff. - S11: PASS (above), including the display-vs-logging distinction requested. - S12: N/A -- no export functionality touched. - S13: N/A, trigger not met (see Migration sign-off above). - S14: N/A -- no Profile/publish_consent code touched; `createWalkinProfile` leaves `publish_consent` at its column default (unset/false). COMMANDS RUN BY ME, REAL OUTPUT: `npm run lint` (repo root) -> exit 0, 0 errors, 2 pre-existing unrelated apps/web LCP warnings (Footer.tsx/Nav.tsx, outside apps/bot, unrelated to this diff). `npm run build` (repo root) -> exit 0, both workspaces (Next.js + bot tsc) clean. `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root) -> 30 files / 300 tests passed, 0 failed. `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism apps/bot/src/handlers/walkin.db.test.ts` alone -> 7/7 passed in 1.42s total, no DB-unreachable skip warning printed, confirming the real-Postgres suite actually ran (not silently skipped). Scope/hygiene: `git status --short` clean before my review; no files modified by me other than this handoff. Verdict: PASS. S1's abandon-at-consent case is structurally true (no write function is reachable before a Confirm/Confirm-override tap); the message-text-as-state-carrier mechanism is independently re-derived as content-forgery-proof from Telegram/grammY's own semantics, and cross-context confirm forgery is separately refused by authorization re-derivation at every tap regardless of message visibility; S2's organizer-only gate is the sole authorization path at all three entry points; S7/S8's capacity/audit atomicity holds via fresh per-call locked transactions; S11's phone-in-audit/log negative case is satisfied structurally, and the phone-display-to-the-same-organizer exception is sound under S11's own third-party-scoped wording; the phone-match false-positive risk is a named, accepted data-integrity tradeoff that does not leak the matched person's identity to the organizer. One non-blocking observational note filed above (pre-existing, bot-wide, not introduced by this diff) about the absence of any chat-type restriction on command dispatch. No blocking defect found across S1-S14.

evidence.s1_abandon_case: makeWalkinCommandHandler performs no write of any kind after all validations pass; commitWalkin (the only write entry point into users/profiles/registrations) is reachable only from the confirm/override callback handlers. Re-ran producer's AC1 test (real DB): /walkin dispatched, confirm message sent, Confirm never tapped, zero rows in users/profiles/registrations.
evidence.message_text_carrier_rederivation: grammY's ctx.callbackQuery.message reflects Telegram-server-stored content; only the bot's own token can attach reply_markup/callback_data to a message or edit its text, so a callback_query matching walkin:confirm:<eventId> can only originate from a message this bot itself rendered for that exact eventId. Independently re-derived from Bot API semantics, not copied from the design gate's conclusion.
evidence.cross_context_forgery_case: eventId for every authorization/write decision comes from the tapped button's callback_data, never from re-parsed message text (parseWalkinMessageFields returns no eventId field at all). requireOrganizerForChapter re-reads the TAPPER's own role/chapterId (via ctx.from.id) and the event's real chapterId fresh on every tap (command, confirm, override) -- an organizer for a different chapter who taps another organizer's confirm message is refused 'wrong-chapter' exactly as if they had typed the command themselves.
evidence.s7_s8_staleness_atomicity: commitWalkin opens its own db.transaction per call, locks the events row and any existing registration row FOR UPDATE, and computes admittedCount/seatsLeft fresh inside that lock -- no value from an earlier tap or handler-level read is ever reused. Exactly one writeAuditLog call exists on each of the two writing branches, in the same transaction as the row mutation.
evidence.s11_log_audit_negative_case: writeAuditLog payloads are exactly {eventId, source} or {eventId, previousAdmission, source} -- phone/name/company are never keys. Zero log./console./logger. calls anywhere in the new/changed code. Success-message interpolation uses only parsedFields.name/company, never phone.
evidence.s11_display_vs_logging: The confirm/override message echoes the raw phone back into the SAME chat the organizer just typed it into, addressed to that same organizer -- not a third party, not a log/error-trace/audit-payload, matching S11's own third-party-scoped wording and REQ-019's formatProfileDump precedent. The phone is never separately logged or audited from the handler layer even though it is re-parsed from the message.
evidence.phone_match_disclosure_case: On a phone match, only the door-typed parsedFields.name/company/phone are ever shown back to the organizer -- getUserIdByPhone returns only an id, no other column, so no field of the matched (possibly wrongly-matched) person's existing profile is ever available to leak. The false-positive risk is a data-integrity tradeoff already named and accepted in the design (§3.3), not a new disclosure.
evidence.observational_note_chat_type: No chat.type/private-chat restriction exists anywhere in apps/bot/src (grepped, zero hits) -- a bot-wide, pre-existing structural assumption, not introduced or worsened by this diff. If /walkin is run in a group chat, the phone would be visible to every member present, not just the organizer. Non-blocking; not filed as a new issue since it predates and is broader than this requirement.
